runs.text:
Contemplate an entangled bank: plants of many kinds cover it, birds sing in the bushes, insects flit about, worms crawl through the damp earth. Laws acting around us produced these elaborately constructed forms, so different from each other, so dependent on each other. Chief among these laws stand Growth, Reproduction, Inheritance, Variability, and a Ratio of Increase so high that it forces a Struggle for Life. From this struggle follows Natural Selection, which entails Divergence of Character and the Extinction of less-improved forms. From the war of nature, from famine and death, follows directly the most exalted object we can conceive: the production of the higher animals.

This view of life holds grandeur. Its several powers were breathed originally into a few forms, or into one. This planet has cycled on according to the fixed law of gravity; from so simple a beginning, endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have evolved, and continue to evolve.
